correctness.rationale: For a support of at least three points the full trace forces an unused symbol in every coordinate; omitting a single point forces that point to have a private coordinate. A binary-valued coordinate can be private for at most one point, and choosing the excluded points' private symbols in their distinct coordinates realizes every trace. Thus the largest possible supports have size three. In each of the 27 binary boxes the eight triangles are precisely the triples in the two parity tetrahedra, and each triple uses both symbols on every axis, fixing its box uniquely. Every pair is shattered; the 162 distance-two pairs each lie in four triangles and the other 189 are maximal. I independently enumerated traces through size four, generated the triangle set via box parity, and eliminated the sparse mod-2 equations on triangle coefficients. Counts were (1,27,351,216,0), with boundary rank 133. The connected complete one-skeleton has boundary rank 26, giving 351−26−133=192 and 216−133=83, with no other reduced homology.
residual_risks: Exact finite mod-2 result only; neither torsion nor integral homotopy type is determined.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact maximal-distance concept class on a basic nonbinary Hamming graph. The private-coordinate structure explains why all pairs but only selected parity triangles are faces. The Betti ranks give a topological comparison beyond equal VC dimension or the shared triangle pattern of a different relation, and the maximal-edge result exhibits nonpurity. These findings do not rely on treating the already known geometric triple pattern as novel.
residual_risks: Small exact instance; no general dimension formula or downstream theorem is established.
